turns.text: *belly low under a sagging plastic tarp, i push into a wall of smell so thick it's almost a sound — hot oil, scorched protein, wet cardboard, a hundred kinds of sweat. tarp drips cold water down my spine one drop at a time. ahead: a forest of legs, boots, wheels, none of them looking down. ears swivel through the noise, sorting it, throwing out the parts that don't matter.*

market row runs three blocks under a patchwork ceiling of tarps and salvaged awning-panels, rain drumming a hundred different rhythms depending on what it's hitting

stalls lean shoulder to shoulder, cook-fires and induction grills throwing heat down at ankle height, close enough for fur to matter, a rare warm current in an otherwise cold night

holo-signs stutter overhead in three languages, none of them yours to read — just color, movement, the occasional crackle-buzz of a projector unit running hot

beneath the crowd-noise: coins of e-yen clicking into a jar, a woman haggling in a flat tired voice, a fryer basket dumped and refilled, and under all of it, low, a floor that never quite stops vibrating — something running underground, something big, patient

*thread between two sets of boots, close enough to feel the heat coming off them, never touching. nose drags along the wet ground, cataloguing — grease, ash, someone's dropped noodle gone cold and abandoned three stalls back not worth the risk. keep moving. a new smell cuts through everything else: seared meat-protein, fresh, still steaming, close.*

the smell's coming off a synth-meat grill two stalls up, vendor's back turned, hands full with a customer's order, sauce ladled loud and sloppy — a fat dripping off-cut just missed the tray and stuck to the stall's underside strut, still sizzling faint

no cam covers this angle, the vendor's own body blocks the overhead unit, and the crowd's legs make a moving wall nothing above waist-height can see through

cook-drone hovers idle at the grill's far end, rotors folded, waiting on a recharge cycle — it won't notice anything under a meter tall

the off-cut hangs there, three body-lengths off, through a gap in the legs that opens and closes with the crowd's shuffle like a held breath

/\/\_/\/\
    (  O   O  )
     \  ^Y^  /
      )=====(      -- ears up, rotor incoming --

*freeze mid-step at a new rotor-whine, higher pitch than the cook-drone, closer, coming in low over the tarps. fur lifts along the spine before the sound even finishes registering. duck sideways under the grill stall's lowest strut, folding small into a gap between a crate and the wall, eyes up, tracking the shape moving against the holo-glow.*

it's not a hunter — a delivery drone, courier-marked, cutting low through the market lane because the wind's too rough above the rooftops tonight, in a hurry, engine straining under a strapped parcel

it clips a hanging string of paper lanterns on its way through, sends them swinging, throws jittering light across the crate you're wedged behind

vendor curses up at it, shakes a fist without looking away from the grill, the moment already forgotten by everyone standing

your gap holds — dry, out of the rain, the off-cut still hanging three body-lengths off, untouched, cooling now, smell going slightly less sharp with every second not spent moving toward it

*wait two more breaths for the rotor-whine to fade behind the tarps, then ease out low and fast, straight line for the off-cut, jaw already opening. mid-stride, a new smell cuts across the meat-smell and stops the legs before the head decides to — bitter, green, deliberate. old scent, laid low along a support post at exactly nose height. not mine. not friendly.*

the post is a market strut for a stall three down, wood softened by years of rain, and someone's worked that bitter-herb mark into the grain deep, reapplied often enough to still be sharp

underneath the herb: fur-scent, lean and hungry, edged with something metallic — a data-jack scar healed wrong, the kind you only get from tapping lines you're not cleared to tap

     ⚠ CROSSING: unfamiliar crew, active claim, edge of grill row

this is a border post, not a home marker — staked out to say *this far and no farther*, the kind of line that gets enforced personally, not by drones

the off-cut's on the near side of it, still in reach, still yours if you're quick and don't linger past the taking

*don't linger. snatch the off-cut in one motion, grease burning warm against the tongue, and turn back the way i came without crossing the post-line, tail low, ears flat, moving like i was never there at all. weight of the meat swinging heavy and good with each stride.*

clean take — the vendor's still turned away, the border scent stays exactly where it was, undisturbed, no reason for anyone on either side of that line to know you passed through it

rain picks up outside the tarp-cover, drumming harder now, driving the thinnest edge of the crowd toward shelter, more legs crowding the lane, more cover

far off, past the stalls, a low mechanical groan rises through the ground — something heavy moving on rails, felt more than heard, vibrating up through four paws before the sound of it ever arrives

the off-cut's still hot enough to steam faintly against the wet air

*drag the off-cut into the dead space behind a stack of empty crates, wedge myself in after it, back to the wall, meat pinned under both paws before the first bite. eating fast but not frantic, ears never fully stopping their sweep — crowd-noise, rain, that low rail-groan building steadier now under everything else.*

crates smell of old fish-crate brine and cardboard gone soft, good cover, tucked out of every sightline that matters

the rail-groan resolves as it gets closer — a monorail car easing along its elevated line two streets over, wheels singing against wet track, headlamp throwing a long white bar across the tarps overhead every few seconds like a slow lighthouse sweep

market noise thins as the rain thickens, half the stalls starting to pull tarps down early, vendors packing induction grills into crates of their own, the night folding itself up around the edges

your off-cut's down to bone and gristle now, and the last of its steam finally gives out

*leave the bone behind, licking grease off one paw before the next move. rain's finding its way through gaps in the tarp now, cold fat drops landing on the back of the neck. push up onto the crate stack, high enough to see past the stall-line — the white sweep of the monorail light keeps passing, steady, dry-looking under its platform roof.*

from the crates, the platform's visible two streets over, raised on concrete stilts, a narrow strip of dry ground under its overhang where the rain can't quite reach at this angle

few people wait there this late, huddled at the far end near the ticket kiosk's warm glow, none of them watching the stairs

between here and there: open wet street, one bad crossing under a streetlamp's cone of light, then a drainage gutter running the last stretch to the platform stairs, deep enough to walk hidden in if you don't mind wet paws

the market's closing down behind you, tarps coming loose, the smell of it already starting to wash thin under the rain

*drop off the crates and angle for the gutter, sticking to the darkest seam of the street, paws already resigned to the cold water. one glance back at the market's shrinking lights, then forward, toward the dry strip and the steady white sweep of the passing rail cars.*

gutter runs shallow and fast, carrying grease-sheen and street-grit down toward a drain grate somewhere out of sight, cold enough to bite at the pads but shallow enough to move through at a trot without swimming for it

the streetlamp's cone comes and goes in under three strides, empty of anyone watching, just wet asphalt and your own shadow stretching long and then gone

platform stairs rise up ahead, concrete beaded with rain, the overhang's dry shadow waiting at the top like a held breath

somewhere above, another monorail car eases in, brakes hissing, and for one long moment the whole platform hums under its own small thunder
